title: Usage Insights API sketches (route/model breakdown + top cost drivers) — working draft
content:
Context / intent
- This doc is intentionally rough: endpoint shapes + sample payloads so Console FE can start wiring tables/drilldowns, and so Telemetry can validate what we can answer cheaply.
- Primary UI: Usage → Cost → “Route & model breakdown” table, with drilldown + “Top cost drivers / What changed?” cards.
- Non-goals (for these sketches): final naming, final error schema, final export lifecycle. Those live in Confluence API contract / CSV spec.


Naming conventions (WIP)
- “route” means canonicalized API route after route normalization (see ADR). Example: "/v1/chat/completions".
- “route_template” is templated path if we ever expose it (e.g., "/v1/projects/{project_id}/…") — NOT planned for initial UI, but may be needed for internal debug.
- “model” is the display model name customers see (e.g., "llama-3.1-70b").
- “model_family” + “model_version” are stable bucketing dimensions; aliases should map to these.


Auth + permissions (placeholder)
- All endpoints require bearer token.
- RBAC gating:
  - viewing cost: role/workspace setting must allow cost visibility
  - exporting: separate permission (stricter) + audit log event
- Important: Console should handle “permitted to view usage but not cost” by either hiding $ fields or returning masked values.


Time semantics
- Console passes time range as [start, end) in ISO-8601 with timezone offset, or a named preset.
- Backend normalizes to UTC for storage/query.
- Buckets are inclusive of bucket start, exclusive of bucket end.


Core endpoint (breakdown table)

GET /v1/usage/insights/breakdown
Purpose
- Return aggregated usage + cost for a time range, grouped by dimensions (route, model, etc.) for table display.

Query params (draft)
- workspace_id: string (required)
- project_id: string (optional)
- environment: "prod" | "staging" | "dev" (optional)
- start: ISO-8601 timestamp (required)
- end: ISO-8601 timestamp (required)
- granularity: "hour" | "day" (optional; default "day")
- group_by: comma-separated dimensions. Initial supported:
  - route
  - model
  - deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private)
  - region
  - cache_status (hit|miss|bypass)  (NOTE: might be too high-cardinality depending on definition)
- filter_* (optional):
  - route
  - model
  - deployment_mode
  - region
- sort_by: "cost_usd" | "tokens_in" | "tokens_out" | "requests" | "latency_ms_p95" (default "cost_usd")
- sort_dir: "asc" | "desc" (default "desc")
- limit: integer (default 50, max 200)
- cursor: opaque string (pagination)
- include: comma-separated extras:
  - "latency" → include latency percentiles
  - "retries" → include retry counts
  - "fallbacks" → include fallback counts
  - "context_length_histogram" → include coarse histogram (see below)

Notes
- To keep totals consistent, response includes an overall totals object that should match billing hooks within tolerance.
- Backend should enforce cardinality guardrails (e.g., max unique routes returned) and return a clear error when exceeded.

Response shape (draft)
{
  "request_id": "req_01J…",
  "freshness": {
    "as_of": "2026-02-07T19:05:00Z",
    "data_lag_seconds": 180,
    "is_partial": false,
    "partial_reason": null
  },
  "currency": "USD",
  "time_range": {"start": "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z", "end": "2026-02-08T00:00:00Z"},
  "group_by": ["route", "model"],
  "filters": {"workspace_id": "ws_9b…", "project_id": "proj_1a…", "environment": "prod"},
  "totals": {
    "cost_usd": 12842.19,
    "requests": 981220,
    "tokens_in": 912381234,
    "tokens_out": 1182234012,
    "cache": {"hit_requests": 120344, "miss_requests": 860876},
    "retries": {"retry_requests": 14432},
    "fallbacks": {"fallback_requests": 3299}
  },
  "rows": [
    {
      "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
      "model": "llama-3.1-70b",
      "cost_usd": 4821.12,
      "requests": 210433,
      "tokens_in": 183920112,
      "tokens_out": 301220552,
      "cache_hit_rate": 0.07,
      "retry_rate": 0.012,
      "fallback_rate": 0.004,
      "latency_ms": {"p50": 410, "p95": 1120, "p99": 1820},
      "context_length": {
        "p50_input_tokens": 820,
        "p95_input_tokens": 4096,
        "buckets": "0-512:12%,513-1024:41%,1025-2048:33%,2049-4096:11%,4097+:3%"
      },
      "notes": ["high token_out per request", "cache hit rate below workspace avg"]
    },
    {
      "route": "/v1/embeddings",
      "model": "bge-m3",
      "cost_usd": 2103.44,
      "requests": 442110,
      "tokens_in": 293920112,
      "tokens_out": 0,
      "cache_hit_rate": 0.36,
      "retry_rate": 0.006,
      "fallback_rate": 0.000
    }
  ],
  "page": {"next_cursor": "eyJvZmZzZXQiOjUw…", "has_more": true}
}

Implementation notes / TODOs
- context_length histogram should likely be opt-in (include=context_length_histogram) and returned as a single encoded string for now (avoids nested arrays; backend stores full histogram).
- latency percentiles should be omitted unless include=latency; computing p99 for large workspaces is expensive.
- Consider returning “cache_status” breakdown fields in a compact form rather than adding a dimension. Example: cache="hit:7%,miss:93%".


Drilldown endpoint (row details)

GET /v1/usage/insights/breakdown/{dimension_value}/details
Purpose
- When user clicks a row, show breakdown drivers for that row (e.g., route+model pair), optionally by time bucket.

Sketch
- dimension_value is not ideal; may change to query-param-based.
- Proposed: keep it query-param-based to avoid weird encoding:

GET /v1/usage/insights/details
Query params (draft)
- workspace_id, start, end (required)
- route, model (required for now)
- by: "day" | "hour" | "none" (default "day")
- include: "cache" | "retries" | "fallbacks" | "streaming" | "latency" | "token_out_distribution"

Response (sample)
{
  "request_id": "req_01J…",
  "freshness": {"as_of": "2026-02-07T19:05:00Z", "data_lag_seconds": 180, "is_partial": false, "partial_reason": null},
  "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
  "model": "llama-3.1-70b",
  "currency": "USD",
  "summary": {
    "cost_usd": 4821.12,
    "requests": 210433,
    "tokens_in": 183920112,
    "tokens_out": 301220552,
    "avg_tokens_out_per_request": 1431.6,
    "streaming": {"streamed_requests": 201112, "streamed_request_rate": 0.956},
    "cache": {"hit_requests": 15012, "miss_requests": 195421},
    "retries": {"retry_requests": 2526},
    "fallbacks": {"fallback_requests": 824}
  },
  "timeseries": [
    "2026-02-01: cost_usd=642.11 requests=28122 tokens_out=39220111 cache_hit_rate=0.08 retry_rate=0.010",
    "2026-02-02: cost_usd=690.44 requests=29701 tokens_out=42112200 cache_hit_rate=0.07 retry_rate=0.011",
    "2026-02-03: cost_usd=701.33 requests=30220 tokens_out=44099110 cache_hit_rate=0.06 retry_rate=0.013"
  ],
  "debug": {"route_normalized": true, "model_bucket": "llama-3.1|70b|2025-12"}
}

Note: timeseries is encoded as strings in this sketch to avoid nested objects in the example. Real API will return structured arrays.


Top cost drivers + “What changed?” endpoint

GET /v1/usage/insights/top-drivers
Purpose
- Return ranked driver explanations for a given scope (workspace/project + optional route/model filters) and time comparison.
- Used for cards: “Top cost drivers” and “What changed since last week?”

Query params (draft)
- workspace_id (required)
- project_id, environment (optional)
- start, end (required)
- compare_to: "previous_period" | "previous_week" | "custom"
- compare_start, compare_end (required if compare_to=custom)
- scope:
  - scope=workspace (default)
  - scope=route (requires route)
  - scope=model (requires model)
  - scope=route_model (requires route and model)
- limit (default 5, max 20)

Driver types (initial shortlist)
- TOKEN_OUT_INCREASE (token_out per request up)
- TOKEN_IN_INCREASE (context length / prompt bloat)
- MODEL_MIX_SHIFT (requests moved to higher-cost model family)
- CACHE_HIT_RATE_DROP (more misses)
- RETRIES_UP (more retry attempts counted as billable compute)
- FALLBACKS_UP (fallback to larger model / cross-region)
- STREAMING_OVERHEAD (if we attribute extra compute per streamed token; TBD)
- LATENCY_SPEND_CORRELATION (spend increase aligned with slower p95 => less batching, more tail)

Response (sample)
{
  "request_id": "req_01J…",
  "freshness": {"as_of": "2026-02-07T19:05:00Z", "data_lag_seconds": 180, "is_partial": false, "partial_reason": null},
  "currency": "USD",
  "scope": {"type": "route_model", "route": "/v1/chat/completions", "model": "llama-3.1-70b"},
  "time_range": {"start": "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z", "end": "2026-02-08T00:00:00Z"},
  "comparison": {"mode": "previous_week", "compare_start": "2026-01-25T00:00:00Z", "compare_end": "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z"},
  "totals": {
    "cost_usd": "current=4821.12 previous=3560.88 delta=1260.24 delta_pct=35.4%",
    "requests": "current=210433 previous=198202 delta=12231 delta_pct=6.2%"
  },
  "drivers": [
    {
      "rank": 1,
      "driver_type": "TOKEN_OUT_INCREASE",
      "headline": "Tokens out per request increased",
      "explanation": "Output tokens/request increased from 1065 → 1432 (+34.4%). This accounts for ~$740 of the $1,260 WoW cost increase.",
      "evidence": "avg_tokens_out_per_request current=1431.6 previous=1064.8",
      "recommended_actions": [
        "Review prompts for verbosity/regression; consider tighter system instructions",
        "Add max_output_tokens caps per route",
        "Run eval on representative prompt set (Optimize → Regressions)"
      ],
      "docs_links": ["/docs/console/usage-insights#tokens-out"]
    },
    {
      "rank": 2,
      "driver_type": "CACHE_HIT_RATE_DROP",
      "headline": "Cache hit rate dropped",
      "explanation": "Cache hit rate dropped from 14% → 7%. Misses increased compute tokens and reduced batching efficiency.",
      "evidence": "cache_hit_rate current=0.07 previous=0.14",
      "recommended_actions": ["Enable prefix caching for this route where safe", "Check if prompts include high-cardinality timestamps/IDs"],
      "docs_links": ["/docs/optimize/caching"]
    },
    {
      "rank": 3,
      "driver_type": "RETRIES_UP",
      "headline": "Retry rate increased",
      "explanation": "Retry requests increased from 0.7% → 1.2%. Retries can double-count compute if the upstream client retries timeouts.",
      "evidence": "retry_rate current=0.012 previous=0.007",
      "recommended_actions": ["Tune client timeout + retry policy", "Investigate upstream 5xx spikes in the same period"],
      "docs_links": ["/docs/console/usage-insights#retries"]
    }
  ],
  "notes": [
    "Estimates are attribution-based and may differ from invoice by rounding/time-window; see reconciliation policy.",
    "Driver contributions are approximate; we cap contribution to total delta and de-duplicate overlaps."
  ]
}

Open question
- Do we want drivers to return stable machine-readable numeric fields (delta_usd, delta_pct, etc.)? Yes for UI sorting, but we must avoid misleading precision. Suggest: return both a number and a rounded display string.


Export endpoint (mention only; full spec elsewhere)

POST /v1/usage/insights/export
- Creates async export job for a given breakdown query.
- Response returns export_job_id.

GET /v1/usage/insights/export/{export_job_id}
- Poll status; when complete, returns signed download URL.

Notes
- Exports must emit audit events (who, what query, download URL issuance, download event if available).
- Exports should enforce size limits (e.g., max rows) and require explicit time range bounds.


Pagination (draft contract)
- Cursor-based pagination only (offset is too expensive on large partitions).
- cursor encodes (sort_by, sort_dir, last_seen_values, time_range_hash) to prevent misuse.
- next_cursor is null when has_more=false.

Potential edge cases
- When underlying data changes between pages (late events), cursor pagination may produce duplicates or skips.
  - Mitigation: use “as_of” freeze timestamp for a query, or accept eventual consistency for beta.


Caching (draft behavior)
- Server-side query cache: Redis (or in-service memory) keyed by normalized request:
  - workspace_id, start/end rounded to minute, filters, group_by, sort/limit/cursor, include.
- Cache TTL targets:
  - breakdown: 30–60s
  - top-drivers: 2–5m (more expensive, less frequently clicked)
- HTTP caching:
  - Set Cache-Control: private, max-age=60 (Console is authenticated; avoid shared caching)
  - Optionally add ETag derived from (as_of + query hash) so FE can revalidate


Error handling (rough)
- 400 invalid params (end <= start, unknown group_by)
- 403 forbidden (cost hidden or export not allowed)
- 413 query too large (time range too long for interactive UI; prompt to reduce)
- 422 cardinality exceeded (route explosion; prompt to add filter)
- 429 rate limit exceeded (export creation)
- 503 freshness/warehouse lag (if data is too stale; include freshness.partial_reason)


Consistency vs Billing
- Console should show a tooltip: “Totals reconcile with billing within tolerance; data may lag by a few minutes.”
- We should expose in the API:
  - reconciliation_status: "ok" | "drift" | "unknown" (optional)
  - drift_pct (rounded) if drift detected


TODO list
- Decide final endpoint paths ("/v1/usage/insights" vs "/v1/insights/usage").
- Confirm which metrics are available at aggregation time vs query time (esp. p99 latency + context hist).
- Confirm definition of retries/fallbacks for attribution:
  - retry_requests = request attempts beyond first? only billable attempts? include client retries?
  - fallback_requests = model routing fallback events? include region fallback?
- Confirm model alias bucketing behavior to prevent duplicate rows (see SUP-24844).
- Confirm route normalization mapping for OpenAI-compat endpoints (see SUP-24827).

Changelog
- 2026-01-12: initial sketches for breakdown + top-drivers
- 2026-01-26: added cursor pagination notes + caching TTL suggestion
- 2026-02-07: added details endpoint idea + expanded driver types
